title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City School Board met Thursday evening and made quick work of a light summer agenda.

Chairman Misty Lindeman called the meeting to order and members approved the agenda and past meeting minutes.

Superintendent John Neubaum reviewed the district’s financial report and highlighted one big expense that’s causing concern — a $7,000 transportation payment. Neubaum said the real issue is that it’s hitting at a time when very little money is coming in. He told the board the district will need to cash in a CD to cover it. He also reminded members they’re still required to provide transportation for a Clay City student who lives in Xenia. Other than those two items, Neubaum said the rest of the financial report looked routine, and the board approved it with no opposition.

In other updates, Neubaum said the district has received one application for the open science teacher position. The applicant has a master’s degree but is not certified. They plan to pursue certification through the Teach Ready program and will work as a substitute in the meantime.

Principal Brian Wattles gave the board an update on junior high sports. He said they don’t have enough players for a junior high baseball team — only seven students have shown interest. They’ll keep signups open until Monday, and Courtney Mitchel will reach out to see if any others want to join, though some may be fifth and sixth graders. Wattles said numbers look good for basketball, volleyball, cheer, track, and cross country. He also noted that Cisne has expressed early interest in a possible sports co-op, but those talks are just getting started.

Neubaum also brought up the ongoing FOIA (Freedom of Information Act) requests the district continues to receive. He said most come from just one or two sources and appear to have a commercial or business purpose. Because responding to them takes up a lot of staff time, he recommended the board consider adopting a fee schedule at a future meeting.

In new business, the board gave first approval to the latest PRESS Policy update. Members approved Bethany Goodrum as the District Librarian, and they also named her Media and Website Coordinator and High School Yearbook Sponsor. The board formally approved Candace Walker as Junior High Scholastic Bowl Coach. They hired Tammy Renee Harris as a full-time substitute assigned to Family and Consumer Sciences, and they voted to release Jennica Parker as substitute kitchen help.

Toward the end of the meeting, Board Member Oliver Bangert addressed his colleagues about the high school. He said the district is clearly losing students and that it’s time for the board to start talking about the future of the high school. He asked that the topic be added to the August agenda. His comments sparked a short discussion about why enrollment is dropping and what the district might do to reverse the trend. Board members agreed they need to look at all their options. Superintendent Neubaum reminded everyone that nothing will happen immediately, but the board should start preparing for any possibility — with the final decision resting with voters in the district.

title: FMH SCHOOL SPORT PHYSICALS
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital, in partnership with Horizon Healthcare, will offer school and sports physicals at no cost.

These physicals offer families the opportunity to obtain required school and sports physicals at no out-of-pocket cost.  Horizon Healthcare providers will visit scheduled schools and communities across southern Illinois to conduct the physicals.

The remaining scheduled times include: Clay City on July 29th from 1 pm to 3 pm, and in Flora on August 6th from Noon to 5 pm.

Students in Cisne may schedule appointments directly through their local Horizon Healthcare Clinic.

For additional information or to schedule an appointment where required, contact Horizon Healthcare or Fairfield Memorial Hospital.

title: CLAY COUNTY FAIR SCHEDULE
full_story:
The Clay County Fair will start one week from today at 4 pm with the 33rd annual 4H BBQ at the REA building.  Menu is a Salt & Strings pork chop, green beans, cheesy potatoes, homemade desert and drink for $12, or $5 for a hot dog meal.  You can pre-purchase tickets from Clay County 4-H members, or you can stop by the extension office at 210 S Church St., Louisville, or you can buy tickets at the door.

Gates will then open at 5:30 for the Crain Scates Bucking Bulls Rodeo hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  Cost to enter the rodeo is $15, those 5 and under get in for free, pre show tickets are available from Young Leaders and are $12.  Mutton busting will be available for $10 with only 30 spots available for children under 80 lbs.  Carnival rides will also open on Friday night.

Saturday morning July 25th starts at 8 am with the poultry and rabbit check in.  The poultry show is at 9 am followed by the 4H and JR Rabbit Show.  All livestock should be on the fairgrounds by 3 pm.  There will also be a mandatory meeting for all livestock exhibitors and vet papers check at 3 pm.  After the meeting livestock weigh in will begin, and the night ends at 7 pm with the open sheep show.

Sunday, July 26th will have the JR Sheep show at 11 am and JR Goat show at Noon.  Registration for the kids pedal tractor pull at 1 pm next to the Merchants building, and the kids pull is at 2 pm, hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The 4H Horse show and JR Horse show is at 2 pm.  The Clay County 4H Federation will have yard games from 5 to 7 pm.  The Clay County Ministerial Alliance program is from 5:30 to 7 pm and there will be a greased pig contest at 7 pm sponsored by UPI Fairfield.

On Monday, July 27th the fair will kick into high gear with the 4H Beef Show at 8 am followed by the JR Beef Show, AITC Activities will be in the Farm Bureau building from 2 to 4 pm.  Then at 5 pm it’s the Mini Livestock Show for those 4 to 8 years of age hosted by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  The night ends with the Little Miss Pageant at 7:30 pm admission is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 19 young ladies vying for the title held by Izzabella Brinkley.

Tuesday will be Nutrien Ag Solutions Day at the fair with giveaways and activities throughout the day.  At 8 am is the 4H Swine show and Open Beef Show, followed by the Sheep Show at 1 pm and the 4H Goat Show at 2:30 pm.  Then at 5 pm will be the Master Showmanship Contest, sponsored by the Clay County Farm Bureau Young Leaders.  On the stage at 7:30 pm will be the Junior Miss Clay County Fair Pageant and Queen pie auction.  Admission to the Junior Miss pageant is $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 10 contestants, Halle Patridge is the current JR Miss.

Wednesday will start at 8 am with the JR Swine Show followed by the Open Goat Show.  DaS zle Dance and Tumble will perform at 5 pm, admission is free, and the 4H Livestock Auction will begin at 6:30pm.

Thursday opens at 8 am with the Open Dairy Show, then at 5 pm Joni’s Power & Grace Tumbling will be in the REA building, admission is free.  The Lickity Split and Legally Sheila concert will be on the stage 7 pm.

The Fair will culminate with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant Friday night, July 31st at 7 pm, with admission $10 for adults and $5 for kids 3 – 10.  There are 13 young ladies vying for the title.  The current Queen is Olivia Haun.

title: MOTORCYCLE SAFETY CLASSES
full_story:
Despite making up less than 3% of Illinois registered vehicles, motorcycles are involved in nearly 15% of fatal crashes, making the Cycle Rider Safety Training Program all the more important for riders.  Illinois has expanded funding for the program by $6 million to increase motorcycle safety classes this year.

Since 1976, when it was established by the Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT), more than 400,000 riders have completed the training program.  Classes have traditionally been offered through colleges and universities and, locally, have been available during the summer at Frontier Community College, Olney Central College, and in Effingham at the Illinois Army National Guard.

The rider safety program offers Illinois residents free safety training courses for riders of all skill levels and experience.  Graduates receive a completion card that waives the Secretary of State motorcycle licensing test and the associated fee.

IDOT recently announced the program is expanding and is seeking new partners to administer the training.  Eligible applicants include nonprofit organizations, local governments, community colleges and universities.

title: COUNTY ACTIVITIES OF EXCELLENCE
full_story:
The American Farm Bureau Federation 2026 County Activities of Excellence (CAE) program is now open for entries to spotlight programs and projects conducted by county Farm Bureaus.  Submissions are due September 1st.

Selected county Farm Bureaus will have the opportunity to showcase their activity at the AFBF Annual Convention, January 8th through 13th in Charlotte, North Carolina.

All applications must be submitted online. Paper or PDF submissions will not be accepted.  Visit the website fb.org/cae and click “APPLY NOW” to access the application portal.  Create a unique user account.  For multi-county submissions, select one county to manage the application.

AFBF will recognize up to 24 individual county activities, including up to four multi-county collaborations.  Winners will receive 4 complimentary registrations to the 2027 AFBF Annual Convention, a booth space at the trade show, and a $4,500 cash stipend to help with travel and exhibit expenses.

title: GRAND AMERICAN
full_story:
Sparta’s World Shooting and Recreational Complex will host the Amateur Trapshooting Association’s 127th Grand American championships this summer.

The Grand American will take place starting July 29th and end on August 8th.  More than 5,000 competitors and spectators from all over the world will take part in and attend the competition.

The World Shooting Complex has hosted the Grand American every year since 2006.

“Hosting the Grand American is a tremendous point of pride for Illinois, and IDNR is grateful for its long-standing partnership with the Amateur Trapshooting Association,” said IDNR interim Director Renee Snow.  “IDNR is committed to supporting this event and ensuring the World Shooting and Recreational Complex remains a national destination for shooting sports and outdoor recreation.”

For a full schedule of events and information about the Amateur Trapshooting Association, visit the association’s website.  For more information about recreation, dining, and event-hosting capabilities at the facility, visit the World Shooting and Recreational Complex’s website.

title: STATE UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES) announced Thursday that the unemployment rate remained at 5.1% in June, unchanged from May, and up .8% from the same month, one year ago, based on data provided by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).  The revised May unemployment rate was 5.1%.

Total nonfarm payrolls saw a fourth consecutive over-the-month increase in June, up 1,500 to 6,164,400.  The May monthly change in payrolls was revised from the preliminary report, from up 6,000 to up 4,100.  The June payroll jobs estimate and unemployment rate reflect activity for the week including the 12th.

The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs increases included: Leisure and Hospitality up 3,000, Professional and Business Services up 2,300 and Private Education and Health Services up 1,600.  The sectors with the largest over-the-month jobs decreases included: Trade, Transportation and Utilities down 4,100, Information down 1,800 and Financial Activities down 1,700.

The number of unemployed persons in June was 329,700, down 2.0% from May, and up 16.1% over the same month one year ago.  The labor force was down 0.3% from May and down 0.9% over-the-year.  The unemployment rate identifies those individuals who are out of work and seeking employment.  An individual who exhausts or is ineligible for benefits is still reflected in the unemployment rate if they actively seek work.

title: AMMONS PLEADS NOT GUILTY
full_story:
State Representative Carol Ammons and her husband, Aaron Ammons, pleaded not guilty Thursday during their initial appearances in federal court in Urbana.

Carol Ammons entered not guilty pleas to all 10 counts in the indictment, while Aaron Ammons pleaded not guilty to the two counts against him.

Following arraignments before US Magistrate Judge Eric I. Long, both defendants were released on personal recognizance bonds after processing.  Prosecutors did not object to the recommendation for their release.  Aaron Ammons objected to certain bond conditions, but the court overruled those objections.

A pretrial conference for both defendants is scheduled for August 24th by video.  Jury selection and trial are set to begin September 22nd before US District Judge Colin S. Bruce in Urbana.

Carol Ammons is charged with 10 federal counts, including eight counts of wire fraud.  Aaron Ammons faces two charges: conspiracy to obstruct justice and obstruction of justice.  Federal prosecutors allege the charges stem from a yearslong scheme involving campaign funds.

title: AI GUIDANCE WRITTEN WITH AI
full_story:
The Illinois State Board of Education released new guidelines recently on how schools should and should not use artificial intelligence in K-12 education.

One of the most notable aspects of the AI guidelines, however, is that it was written with help from popular AI programs including ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

Bill Curtin, Illinois policy director for the nonprofit advocacy group Teach Plus, one of the groups that pushed for the guidance, called that an example of how AI should be treated in academic fields.

“Upfront, they said, ‘We did use AI,’ and they were very clear and specific about how they used AI,” Curtin told Capitol News Illinois.  “And that actually builds trust because these days you can look at almost anything that anyone writes and wonder if it’s AI.  It’s much better when, upfront, you say: ‘We did use AI, and here’s where, and here’s where the human element is really still seen in this guidance.’”

title: BACK TO SCHOOL VACCINE CLINICS
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is having a series of Back-to-School vaccine clinics.

The next clinic is tomorrow, from 8:30 am to 5 pm at the Health Department on 12th Street.  Appointments are not necessary but are appreciated.  Appointments can be made by calling 618-662-4406.

Illinois state law requires certain immunizations for children and adults enrolled in childcare, school, or college.  State law also mandates immunizations for adults in specific fields of work.

There will also be Back-to-School vaccine clinics on Thursday, July 23rd from 8:30 am to 5 pm; on August 3rd, 6th, 12th, and 13th from 8:30 am to 6 pm.  The final clinic will be from Friday, August 14th from 8 am to Noon.

Again, appointments are not necessary, but appreciated, if you have questions call the Clay County Health Department at 618-662-4406.
